name: Event Organization Portal - SIA Project 21 22
description:
The system is a web portal designed to support people who want to organize an event by bringing together, in a single platform, information about event guests and the various services required for the event.

The platform supports three main types of users: event organizers, service providers, and invited guests.

Service providers register on the platform by providing authentication credentials, personal information, and company details, including VAT number, company address, and accepted payment methods.

Once registered, providers can publish the services offered by their company. Each service belongs to a category, such as catering, hairdressing, florist services, or transportation. For each service, the provider can configure a virtual showcase containing demonstration photos, prices, and the time slots during which the service is available.

Event organizers register by providing credentials, personal information, residence information, their fiscal code, and an IBAN that can be used for service payments.

Through the portal, organizers can create an event by specifying the event type, date, location, and the planned budget. During event creation, they can also select from a predefined list the categories of services for which they want to receive support.

Organizers can add invited guests to the event by entering their personal information, email address, and guest category, such as relative, friend, or colleague. For each invited guest, the system generates an invitation code that is sent by email and is used by the guest as a password to access the platform.

Each event has an associated blog where both organizers and invited guests can publish information about the event, upload photos or videos, create new posts, and comment on existing posts.

After creating an event, the organizer can browse the service showcases provided by suppliers for the selected service categories. The organizer can then request an appointment with a provider by choosing a time compatible with the provider's availability and specifying appointment details and any special requests.

Providers can view appointment requests through their interface and decide whether to approve them. Approved appointments are automatically displayed in a calendar associated with the event, which the organizer can consult to view all confirmed service appointments.

After an appointment between the organizer and the provider has taken place, the provider prepares a quotation for the agreed service and uploads the corresponding amount to the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once a quotation has been uploaded, the organizer can accept or reject it. If the quotation is accepted, its total amount is deducted from the remaining event budget.

When accepting a quotation, the organizer selects both the payment schedule, which can consist of installments, deposit plus final balance, or full payment, and the payment method, which can be online or on-site.

If payment is made on-site, the provider confirms the received amount through the portal. If payment is divided into multiple installments, the provider confirms each received installment separately.

At any time, the organizer can consult the history of contracts associated with the event, including their status and cost, and can also view the remaining event budget.

highLevelGoals: To define the scope, logistics, and financial constraints of the event by specifying type, date, location, and budget.
To curate the attendee list by adding personal details and categories for invited guests.
To identify and select suitable vendors by browsing service showcases within specific categories.
To schedule service delivery by requesting appointments that align with provider availability.
To finalize service agreements by reviewing and accepting or rejecting provider quotations.
To settle financial obligations by selecting payment schedules and methods for accepted services.
To monitor financial health and contractual status by reviewing contract history and remaining budget.
To establish a professional presence on the platform by registering company details and credentials.
To market services by publishing categorized showcases with pricing, photos, and availability.
To manage workload by reviewing and approving or rejecting appointment requests from organizers.
To formalize service delivery by uploading quotations associated with completed appointments.
To ensure financial reconciliation by confirming receipt of payments or installments through the portal.
To securely access event-specific information using a unique invitation code.
lowLevelGoals: Create a new event record by submitting the event type, start date, end date, location, total budget, and preferred payment method (online or on-site).
Add a new guest to the event by providing their full name, email address, and guest category (e.g., VIP, Standard).
Update the guest category for an existing guest record by specifying the guest ID and the new category.
Retrieve a list of service providers filtered by a specific service category (e.g., catering, photography) and location.
Submit a request for a service appointment specifying the provider ID, desired date, and time slot.
Review a specific service quotation and submit an approval or rejection decision with optional comments.
Select a payment method (e.g., credit card, bank transfer) and schedule (e.g., lump sum, installments) for an approved service contract.
Retrieve the current remaining budget, a list of active contracts with their real-time financial status, and any pending payment confirmation notifications for the event.
Register a new company profile by submitting company name, contact details, and business credentials.
Publish a new service showcase by providing the service title, category, description, pricing, and availability calendar.
Configure available time slots for a specific service showcase by defining start and end times and recurring patterns.
Review an incoming appointment request and submit an approval or rejection decision.
Upload a service quotation document and associate it with a specific completed appointment ID.
Confirm the receipt of a specific payment installment by marking the transaction as received in the system.
Access the event portal by submitting a unique invitation code to retrieve event details and blog access.

baselineCritiques.actors: The actors defined are appropriate for the system described. All three main user types (Event Organizer, Service Provider, Invited Guest) are correctly identified based on the software description.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the system's description. All goals are functional, relevant to the actors, and cover key aspects of event organization, service provision, and guest access. No contradictions or omissions were found.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-aligned with the high-level goals and actors, covering all necessary functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the payment method selection (online vs. on-site) during event creation, which is mentioned in the software description but not explicitly addressed in the low-level goals under "Define Event Parameters." Additionally, while the low-level goals cover most functionalities, they could be more precise in some cases (e.g., "Configure Service Time Slots" lacks details on how time slots are defined or validated). The system's description also mentions fiscal code and IBAN for organizers, which should ideally be reflected in the low-level goals under "Register Company Profile" for event organizers. Lastly, the payment confirmation process for providers could benefit from more granularity (e.g., distinguishing between full payments vs. installments).
